transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess the main reason I’m here is that I'm just having this huge problem at work with anything that takes, you know, real sitting-down brain work. Like doing the monthly reports. 

Actually, speaking of those, we just had the state health inspectors come through my clinic last Tuesday, and let me tell you, the lead inspector was a real piece of work. He spent like forty-five minutes just looking at the fire extinguisher tags in the main hallway. I mean, I get it, safety first, but forty-five minutes? My front desk coordinator was just rolling her eyes the whole time, and we had patients backing up into the waiting room because he was blocking the hall. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the reports. Yeah, so things like that, or if I have to sit down and plan a multi-site health event for the network, it just feels like I hit a massive wall. I just keep putting it off and finding other things to do, even when I know it really matters and my bosses are waiting on it.
Did you have this kind of trouble with focus and finishing tasks when you were a child?

Yeah, actually, I really did. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers were always telling my parents at conferences that I was a bright kid, but that I was just constantly daydreaming. I was always losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework. Honestly, the only way anything ever made it back to the teacher was if my mother physically went through my backpack every single night. 

And man, that backpack... it was this classic navy blue Jansport, you know the ones with the brown suede leather on the bottom? I loved that thing. I actually ironed a bunch of patches on it, including this vintage NASA patch my uncle got me when he took a trip down to Florida. He was a huge space nerd, always talking about the Apollo missions and trying to get me to watch these incredibly long, dry documentaries about the moon landing whenever he visited. Honestly, I think he just liked having an excuse to buy that weird freeze-dried astronaut ice cream from the museum gift shops. I tried the Neapolitan one once and it was basically just colored chalk. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, so if my mom didn't empty out that backpack every night, my homework was basically gone forever.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like it’s hard to stay seated or still?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have to be bouncing off the walls or anything. I can sit through a meeting just fine. Well, mostly fine. We actually had this massive network-wide meeting last month about the new electronic health record system they're rolling out. And let me tell you, the vendor they brought in to do the training was just... wow. He was wearing this incredibly loud plaid suit, like something a used car salesman from the seventies would wear, and he kept using all these ridiculous corporate buzzwords. "Synergize the workflow," "leverage the data silos." I was sitting next to our head of IT, and I swear, every time the guy said "paradigm shift," she would just sigh this deep, heavy sigh and aggressively click her pen. It was a really nice pen, actually, one of those heavy metal ones that feel good in your hand. I think it was a Cross pen. I used to have one of those, but I left it at a coffee shop... 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, being fidgety. No, I don't really have a problem staying in my chair. It's more just my brain that won't stay put, you know?
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I don't really sit around stressing about things all day. I mean, my wife, she's a completely different story. She worries enough for both of us. Just last week, she was absolutely convinced that our basement was going to flood because we had that string of heavy rainstorms. She made me go down there like three times a day to check the sump pump. And honestly, our basement is mostly just boxes of old stuff anyway. We have this one huge box that's just full of old VHS tapes. Do you remember those? I don't even know why we still have them. We don't even own a VCR anymore. I think there's a bunch of old family home videos in there, but there's also just random stuff I recorded off the TV in the nineties. Like, I think I have the entire first season of ER on tape somewhere. George Clooney was so young back then. 

But um... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really get anxious or worry about a bunch of different things. My mind is just usually off somewhere else.
